exp: It's the ISD's monthly return showing credit received and how it was distributed.
Filing by the 13th lets the credit reach recipients' 2B generated on the 14th.

options: ITC on input services only, not goods or capital goods
ITC on goods and capital goods
exp: Goods and capital goods are billed to the unit that receives them.

q: A company's head office in Maharashtra receives an invoice of ₹10 lakh + ₹1.8 lakh GST for an audit covering branches in five states. From April 2025, how does the credit reach the branches?
options: The head office keeps all of it
Through its ISD registration and GSTR-6, since ISD became mandatory for common input services
Each branch claims it from the auditor's invoice
exp: Finance Act 2024 made ISD compulsory for such services from 1 April 2025, including services taxed under reverse charge.

q: How is credit on a service used by several branches distributed?
options: In proportion to each of those branches' turnover in the state for the relevant period
exp: Only units that actually use the service share in it.
ref: CGST Act, s.20; CGST Rules, r.39

q: An ISD receives an invoice for a software licence used only by the Pune unit. How is the credit distributed?
exp: Credit attributable to one recipient goes only to that recipient.

q: An ISD's units had FY 2024-25 turnover of ₹6 crore (Delhi), ₹3 crore (Karnataka) and ₹1 crore (Gujarat). In May 2025 it gets ₹2 lakh of ITC on an ad campaign benefiting all three. How much goes to Karnataka?
exp: ₹2 lakh × 3/10. The relevant period is the previous financial year when all the recipients had turnover in it.

q: When must an ISD distribute the credit it receives?
options: In the same month it becomes available, through GSTR-6
exp: Credit can't be parked at the ISD.

options: A read-only statement of the ISD's inward invoices, drawn from suppliers' GSTR-1
exp: It's to the ISD what GSTR-2A is to a normal taxpayer.

q: A branch asks where its ISD credit shows up and how to claim it. What do you tell it?
options: In its GSTR-2B (from the ISD's GSTR-6), claimed in 3B Table 4(A)(4)
exp: If the ISD files late, the credit slips into the branch's next 2B.

q: An ISD wrongly distributed ₹80,000 of credit to the Gujarat unit that belonged to the Delhi unit. What's the fix and what's the risk?
model: Issue an ISD credit note to Gujarat to take the credit back and an ISD invoice to Delhi, both reported in GSTR-6. If Gujarat has already used the credit, it has to reverse it. Credit distributed in excess or to the wrong unit can be recovered from the recipient with interest under s.21, so fixing it before the department spots it matters.
points: ISD credit note to the wrong unit
Fresh distribution to the right unit through GSTR-6
The recipient reverses credit it already used
Wrong distribution is recoverable with interest under s.21
exp: The recovery falls on the recipient unit, not only the ISD.
